symptom:
New client PCs added to the network fail to obtain an automatic IP address via
 DHCP, resulting in an APIPA address (169.254.x.x) and complete lack of local or remote connectivity.
topology_note:
Router0 (2911 acting as DHCP Server) connected via Gi0/0 to Switch0 subnet
192.168.10.0/24; PC2 connected to Switch0 port Fa0/3 set to DHCP.
show_outputs: show ip dhcp pool -> Leased addresses: 0; ipconfig -> Autoconfiguration IPv4 Address 169.254.x.x
expected_root_cause: DHCP service is disabled globally on the router.
fix_steps:
configure terminal -> service dhcp -> end -> 
copy running-config startup-config

symptom: Static route configured with incorrect next-hop IP address results in complete traffic drop and "Request timed out" when pinging remote subnet.
topology_note:
Router0 connected via GigabitEthernet0/1 to Router1 (WAN link 10.0.0.0/30); 
local subnet 192.168.10.0/24 trying to reach remote network 192.168.20.0/24.
show_outputs: show ip route -> Static route lists invalid next-hop IP (e.g., 10.0.0.99 instead of 10.0.0.2).
expected_root_cause: Static route configured with an invalid or unreachable next-hop IP address
fix_steps:
configure terminal -> no ip route 192.168.20.0 255.255.255.0 10.0.0.99 ->  ip route 192.168.20.0 255.255.255.0 10.0.0.2 -> 
end -> copy running-config startup-config

show_outputs:
show vlan brief -> FastEthernet0/2 assigned to VLAN 20 instead of VLAN 10; show interfaces fastethernet0/2 switchport ->

Access port VLAN assignment mismatch isolating the host from 
its router subinterface gateway

config startup-config

symptom: Hosts in VLAN 10 (192.168.10.0/24) cannot ping devices or servers in VLAN 20 (192.168.20.0/24), resulting in "Request timed out" messages.
topology_note:
Router0 connected via GigabitEthernet0/1 to Switch0 subnet 192.168.10.0/24 and 
192.168.20.0/24 using subinterfaces.
show_outputs: show ip interface gigabitethernet0/0.10 -> Outbound access list is 100; show access-lists -> Extended IP access list 100 deny icmp any any
expected_root_cause:
An active Access Control List (ACL) is explicitly denying ICMP (ping) 
traffic between VLAN subnets.
fix_steps:
configure terminal -> interface GigabitEthernet0/0.10 -> 
no ip access-group 100 out -> no access-list 100 -> end -> copy running-config startup-config

show_outputs: show ip dhcp pool VLAN10_POOL -> DNS server: 192.168.10.254; nslookup www.example.com -> Server: Unreachable / DNS request timed out.

symptom: PC connected to Switch port FastEthernet0/1 suddenly loses network connectivity, and the port status shows as down.
topology_note:
Switch0 port FastEthernet0/1 has port-security enabled with a maximum limit of 1 MAC 
address; an unauthorized device or hub was connected to the port, causing a security violation.
show_outputs:
show interfaces fastethernet0/1 -> FastEthernet0/1 is down, line protocol is down (err-disabled); show port-security interface fastethernet0/1 -> 
Port Status: Secure-down, Violation Mode: Shutdown.
expected_root_cause:
Switch port entered the err-disabled state because a port-security violation 
occurred when an unauthorized MAC address exceeded the allowed limit.
fix_steps:
configure terminal -> interface fastethernet0/1 -> shutdown -> 
no shutdown -> switchport port-security maximum 2 -> end -> copy running-config startup-config

symptom:
Client PCs configured for DHCP successfully obtain an automatic IPv4 address from the router's DHCP pool, but experience 100% packet loss and "Request timed out" when attempting to ping their 
default gateway or any remote networks.
topology_note:
Router0 (2911) connected to Switch0 via GigabitEthernet0/0; subnet 192.168.10.0/24; 
Router0 configured as DHCP server for VLAN 10, but the default-router command is missing from the DHCP pool configuration.
show_outputs: show running-config -> default-router statement missing from ip dhcp pool VLAN10_POOL; C:> ipconfig -> Default Gateway field is blank or missing.
expected_root_cause:
DHCP pool configuration is missing the default-router statement, leaving client PCs 
without a gateway address to forward traffic outside their local subnet
fix_steps:
configure terminal -> ip dhcp pool VLAN10_POOL -> default-router 
192.168.10.1 -> end -> copy running-config startup-config

symptom: Inter-VLAN communication fails with 100% packet loss because router subinterfaces lack VLAN encapsulation mapping.
topology_note:
Router0 (2911) connected to Switch0 via Gi0/0; subinterfaces GigabitEthernet0/0.10 and 
GigabitEthernet0/0.20 configured without encapsulation dot1q.
show_outputs: show running-config -> Subinterfaces show IP addresses but omit encapsulation dot1q configuration strings.
expected_root_cause:

correctly tagged and routed between VLANs.

symptom: Workstations cannot access web services (HTTP/HTTPS) due to restrictive packet filtering, despite successful ping connectivity.
topology_note:
Router0 subinterface GigabitEthernet0/0.10 has an active ACL blocking TCP ports 80 and 
443.
show_outputs: show access-lists -> 100 deny tcp any any eq www.
expected_root_cause:
An overly restrictive Access Control List (ACL) rule blocks Layer 4 HTTP/HTTPS 
traffic between subnets.
fix_steps:
configure terminal -> no ip access-group 100 in -> no access-list 100 -> ip access-list extended 100 -> permit
 tcp any any eq www -> permit ip any any -> interface gigabitethernet0/0.10 -> ip access-group 100 in -> end -> copy running-config startup-config

symptom: New devices fail to receive IP addresses, receiving APIPA (169.254.x.x) addresses due to exhausted lease pools.
topology_note: Router0 DHCP pool capacity is fully utilized with zero available addresses remaining.
show_outputs: show ip dhcp pool -> IP addresses leased: 254 (100%).
expected_root_cause:
DHCP pool exhaustion caused by a restricted subnet range or missing exclusion
 boundaries.
fix_steps:
ip dhcp pool VLAN20-Pool -> network 192.168.20.0
 255.255.255.0 -> lease 2 -> ip dhcp excluded-address 192.168.20.1 192.168.20.20 -> end -> copy running-config startup-config

symptom: Wireless clients associate with the SSID but fail authentication and IP assignment due to security key/encryption mismatches.
topology_note: Wireless-Laptop profile encryption parameters do not match WRT300N wireless settings.
show_outputs: PC Wireless status -> Authentication failed / IP configuration timeout (APIPA).
expected_root_cause:
Wireless security mode, encryption type, or pre-shared key mismatch 
between client profile and access point.
fix_steps:
Update wireless client profile -> Select matching SSID (CorpNet) -> 
Configure WPA2-PSK with AES encryption -> Enter correct pre-shared key -> Verify DHCP IP assignment.

symptom: VLAN name or port description discrepancy causing documentation/management mismatches while data forwarding remains fully operational.
topology_note:
Switch0 VLAN 20 database name or interface description does not match corporate naming 
standard.
show_outputs: VLAN 20 name differs from network documentation; show interfaces description -> Generic interface label.
expected_root_cause: Administrative documentation oversight or VLAN naming typo on the switch.

-> Save configuration (copy running-config startup-config).

symptom: Internal hosts fail to reach external networks due to missing or misconfigured NAT overload (PAT) rules, while local routing succeeds.
topology_note:
Router0 lacks proper interface NAT bindings (ip nat inside/outside) or dynamic source 
translation overload commands.
show_outputs: show ip nat translations -> Empty table; show ip nat statistics -> Zero active translations.
expected_root_cause:
Missing Network Address Translation Overload (PAT) configuration or incorrect inside/
outside interface assignments on the edge router.
fix_steps:
Access router CLI -> Define access list for internal subnet -> Configure ip nat inside source list interface 
overload -> Assign ip nat inside and ip nat outside to respective interfaces -> Save configuration.

symptom: Clients fail to resolve domain names to correct IP addresses due to static record typos, while direct IP communication succeeds.
topology_note:
Server0 or router contains a misconfigured static host mapping table entry pointing
 to an invalid IP address.
show_outputs: nslookup intranet.corp.local -> Non-existent domain / incorrect IP resolution.
expected_root_cause: Static DNS record typographical error or incorrect IP binding in the local name resolution table.
fix_steps:
Access server/router CLI -> Remove incorrect host binding ->
 Configure correct ip host entry with valid server IP -> Save configuration.
Concept_Tag: Static DNS Record Management & Name Resolution

symptom: Workstations fail to acquire dynamic IP addresses, receiving APIPA addresses due to pool exhaustion or overlapping static IP assignments.
topology_note:
Router DHCP pool lacks proper excluded address ranges for static infrastructure IPs,
 causing allocation failures.
show_outputs: show ip dhcp binding / show ip dhcp pool -> Pool exhaustion or overlapping leases.
expected_root_cause: Missing or incorrectly configured ip dhcp excluded-address commands on the gateway router.
fix_steps:
Access router CLI -> Configure excluded address ranges ->
 Re-define DHCP pool -> Clear existing bindings -> Save configuration.
Concept_Tag: Dynamic Host Configuration Protocol & Address Pool Management

symptom: Workstation communicates locally on the VLAN but cannot reach remote subnets or gateway due to an incorrect gateway IP configured on the host.
topology_note: PC0 default gateway address is misconfigured with a typo (192.168.10.254 instead of 192.168.10.1).
show_outputs: ipconfig /all -> Default Gateway mismatch with router interface IP.
expected_root_cause: Incorrect default gateway IP address manually configured on the client host interface.
fix_steps:
Access host IP configuration -> Update Default Gateway to match
 router interface IP -> Test ping connectivity.
Concept_Tag: Host IP Configuration & Default Gateway Management

symptom: Remote subnets unreachable due to an incorrect subnet mask configured on a static route.
topology_note: Static route on Router0 has a subnet mask typo (255.255.0.0 vs 255.255.255.0).
show_outputs: show ip route -> Subnet mask mismatch on static route entry.
expected_root_cause: Typographical error in the subnet mask of a manually configured static route.
fix_steps:
Enter global config -> Remove bad static route (no ip route) ->
 Add correct static route -> Save config (copy running-config startup-config).

symptom: Network experiences intermittent broadcast storms and loops due to unstable root bridge elections.
topology_note: Redundant switches configured with default STP priorities causing election conflicts.
show_outputs: show spanning-tree -> Unstable root bridge role assignment across switches.
expected_root_cause: Missing or conflicting Spanning Tree Protocol (STP) priority configurations.
fix_steps:
Enter global config -> Configure explicit bridge priority (spanning-
tree vlan 1 priority 4096) -> Save config (copy running-config startup-config).
Concept_Tag: Spanning Tree Protocol (STP) Root Bridge Election

symptom: PC0 and Server0 intermittently lose connectivity; ARP table shows flapping MAC addresses.
topology_note: Two hosts manually configured with the same static IP.
show_outputs: show arp / arp -a -> Same IP mapped to two different MACs.
expected_root_cause: Duplicate IP assignment on the subnet.
fix_steps:
Check ARP cache -> Inspect IP configurations -> Reconfigure 
one host with a unique IP -> Verify with ping and arp -a.

symptom: Wireless clients experience frequent disconnections and slow throughput due to high interference.
topology_note: Two APs configured on overlapping channels (both on channel 6).
show_outputs: Wireless survey / show ap channels -> High interference detected on channel 6.
expected_root_cause: Overlapping Wi-Fi channels causing co-channel interference.
fix_steps:
Inspect channel configuration -> Identify overlap -> Reconfigure
 one AP to use channel 1 or 11 -> Verify stable connectivity.

symptom: Wireless clients cannot discover the SSID automatically due to broadcast suppression.
topology_note: AP-Guest configured with SSID broadcast disabled.
show_outputs: GUI Wireless Settings -> SSID broadcast parameter set to Disabled.
expected_root_cause: SSID broadcast suppression causing minor onboarding friction.
fix_steps:
Open Wireless Router GUI -> Navigate to Basic Wireless 
Settings -> Change SSID Broadcast to Enabled -> Click Save Settings -> Verify automatic network discovery via client site survey.
